rows.question: With reference to Figure 1-8: Time, Distance and Fuel to Climb, departure airfield elevation 1380 ft, QNH 1009 hPa, temperature is standard, cruise pressure altitude 7500 ft, temperature ISA+12°C. The distance covered during the climb is approximately:

before.explanation:
GIVEN
Departure airfield elevation 1380 ft, QNH 1009 hPa, temperature standard; cruise pressure altitude 7500 ft, temperature ISA+12 deg C. Distance covered during the climb to be found.

METHOD (SACAA-01 Figure 1-8, Time, Distance and Fuel to Climb)
Step 1: Convert departure elevation to pressure altitude: PA = 1380 + (1013 - 1009) x 30 = 1500 ft; ISA temperature there = 15 - (2 x 1.5) = 12 deg C.
Step 2: At 7500 ft, ISA temperature = 15 - (2 x 7.5) = 0 deg C, so cruise OAT = 0 + 12 = 12 deg C.
Step 3: Enter at +12 deg C / 1500 ft, transfer up to the DISTANCE - NM line and read the cumulative distance at the departure condition; enter again at +12 deg C / 7500 ft and read the cumulative distance at the cruise condition.
Step 4: Subtract the departure reading from the cruise reading to get the distance covered during the climb.

ANSWER
20 NM

after.explanation:
GIVEN
Departure airfield elevation 1380 ft, QNH 1009 hPa, temperature standard
Cruise pressure altitude 7500 ft, temperature ISA +12°C
Find the distance covered during the climb

METHOD (SACAA-01 Figure 1-8, Time, Distance and Fuel to Climb)
Step 1: Departure pressure altitude and temperature
PA = 1380 + (1013 − 1009) × 30 = 1500 ft
ISA temperature = 15 − (2 × 1.5) = 12°C

Step 2: Cruise temperature at 7500 ft
ISA temperature = 15 − (2 × 7.5) = 0°C
Cruise OAT = 0 + 12 = 12°C

Step 3: Read the chart twice
Enter at +12°C and 1500 ft, go up to the DISTANCE (NM) line and read the distance at departure.
Enter again at +12°C and 7500 ft and read the distance at cruise.

Step 4: Subtract
Climb distance = cruise reading − departure reading

ANSWER
20 NM

rows.question: With reference to Figure 1-22: Take-off distance, pressure altitude 3500 ft, weight 2400 lb, temperature +20°C, 4 kt tailwind. The take-off ground roll is:

before.explanation:
GIVEN
Pressure altitude 3500 ft, weight 2400 lb, temperature +20°C, 4 kt tailwind. Take-off ground roll.

METHOD (SACAA-01 Figure 1-22)
Step 1: Enter the Take-off Performance Table at +20°C.
Step 2: At +20°C, Ground Roll reads 1190 ft at PA 3000 ft and 1310 ft at PA 4000 ft. PA 3500 ft is exactly midway.
Step 3: Apply the tailwind footnote: increase all distances by 10% for each 2 kt of tailwind (here 4 kt = 20%).

SOLVE
Interpolate Ground Roll: (1190+1310)/2 = 1250 ft
Apply 4 kt tailwind (+20%): 1250 x 1.20 = 1500 ft

ANSWER
1500 ft

after.explanation:
GIVEN
Pressure altitude 3500 ft, weight 2400 lb, temperature +20°C, 4 kt tailwind
Find the take-off ground roll

METHOD (SACAA-01 Figure 1-22)
Step 1: Enter the Take-off Performance Table at +20°C.
Step 2: Ground roll reads 1190 ft at PA 3000 ft and 1310 ft at PA 4000 ft. PA 3500 ft is exactly midway.
Step 3: Tailwind footnote: add 10% for each 2 kt of tailwind, so 4 kt adds 20%.

SOLVE
Ground roll at 3500 ft (midway)
(1190 + 1310) ÷ 2 = 1250 ft

With the 4 kt tailwind (+20%)
1250 × 1.20 = 1500 ft

ANSWER
1500 ft

rows.question: With reference to Figure 1-24, weight 2400 lb, aerodrome elevation 2650 ft, QNH 1018 hPa and temperature +24°C. The landing distance required to clear 50 ft is approximately:

before.explanation:
GIVEN
Weight 2400 lb, elevation 2650 ft, QNH 1018 hPa, OAT +24°C.

SOLVE
Pressure altitude = 2650 + (1013 − 1018) × 30 = 2500 ft
Figure 1-24, halfway between 2000 ft and 3000 ft: 1367.5 ft at +20°C and 1402.5 ft at +30°C
+24°C is 0.4 of the way from +20°C to +30°C: 1367.5 + 0.4 × 35 = 1381.5 ft ≈ 1382 ft

ANSWER
1382 ft

Exam tip: Convert elevation to pressure altitude before entering a performance table.
